# Print list

**Generated by [`scripts/900_print_list.py`](../scripts/900_print_list.py) — do not edit by
hand.** Every number here is measured off the exported STLs in `stl/` and `stl_R/`; the mass and
time figures are models, stated below, and should be corrected against the first real print.

17 parts per leg, **34 for the pair**. They are not 15 parts printed twice: each one is chiral,
so a left part cannot be used on the right leg. The engraved number says which — `P5L` against
`P5R` — and that is the only thing distinguishing two parts that otherwise look identical.

## Before you assemble anything: holes

A printed hole comes off the bed 0.1–0.3 mm **under** its modelled size, and any hole whose axis
is not along the build direction prints as an egg. Almost every hole in this device runs along the
knee axis (Z) while most parts build along Y, so **assume every hole needs a drill pass**. Sizes
to finish to, from [`scripts/417_fastener_audit.py`](../scripts/417_fastener_audit.py):

| Modelled | Finish to | What it takes |
|---|---|---|
| ⌀4.2 | 4.3 | M4 clearance |
| ⌀5.0 | 5.0 H7 | locating dowel — ream, do not drill |
| ⌀5.2 | 5.3 | M5 clearance |
| ⌀6.4 | leave as printed | M5 heat-set insert, OD ~7.0, melted in |
| ⌀10.4 | leave as printed | cap head counterbore |
| ⌀12.3 | 12.3 | knee pin through the hub — the joint axis, so do it on a drill press |
| ⌀26 | 26.2 | the two idler bearing seats in the bracket. Bonded, same reason |
| ⌀28 | 28.2 | the 6001 seat in the yoke. 28.2, not 28.0: the bearing is **bonded**, and that |
| | | 0.2 is the bond line. A press fit into PETG creeps and lets go within months |

| Part | Holes |
|---|---|
| `A7_DriveBracket_Idler` | 4 x M4 clearance, 2 x dia 26 idler bearing seats (bond), screw bore |
| `P1_KneeYoke` | 2 x M4 clearance, 6 x M5 clearance, 1 x dia 28 bearing seat (bore 28.2, bond) |

## Where the supports are

Support fraction is of TOTAL surface area, so 10% is a few bosses rather than a disaster. What
matters is a part that cannot be oriented below the threshold at all. Measured, per part over 8%:

* **`A7_DriveBracket_Idler`** — 10% of its surface, 60.6 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+X up, 0°).
* **`P20_KneeCap`** — 9% of its surface, 25.7 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Y up, 0°).
* **`P23a_FairingMount`** — 13% of its surface, 4.4 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Z up, 0°).
* **`P23b_FairingMount`** — 13% of its surface, 4.4 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Z up, 0°).
* **`P23c_FairingMount`** — 13% of its surface, 4.4 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Z up, 0°).
* **`P25_MotorNacelle`** — 10% of its surface, 59.4 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Y up, 0°).
* **`P2a_KneeHub_Pulley29T`** — 12% of its surface, 58.5 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Y up, 0°).
* **`P31_InterfaceDist`** — 10% of its surface, 7.5 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Y up, 0°).
* **`P3_GantryPlate_Printed`** — 13% of its surface, 46.7 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Y up, 0°).
* **`TEST_ToothCoupon_3xHTD8M`** — 14% of its surface, 2.1 cm², overhangs past 45° in its best orientation
  (+Z up, 0°).

The three fairing mounts are one part printed three times, and 4.0 of their 4.4 cm² is in the
first 4 mm above the bed: that is the bracket's foot, a flat underside. Printed on that face
the support disappears — the orientation search cannot see it, because it scores angles and a
flat underside at the bottom of a part is an angle like any other.

For the rest, the cause is not diagnosed here. The figures above say where to look in the
slicer; they do not say what the geometry is doing, and this file is generated, so it should not
guess. An earlier version of this script asserted the fairing mounts' explanation for every part
over 10%, which made it wrong about `P25_MotorNacelle` and `P2a_KneeHub_Pulley29T`.

## The models

The mass model is shell-plus-infill: shell = perimeters × 0.42 mm per side, and any part whose
mean wall (2V/A) is thinner than two shells prints effectively solid regardless of infill. The
time model is volumetric: 3.5 mm³/s of effective flow, which is 0.2 mm layers at 0.42 mm width
and 60 mm/s, derated for travel and acceleration. Neither has been checked against a real print,
because nothing has been printed yet. Correct them here once something has.
